title: Getting Started with LYS: Label Your Song
text: LYS (Label Song) R package recording management, session assignment, tracking interaction multiple vocal components across behavioral experiments. designed researchers record birdsong (vocalizations) across many sessions need automatically detect, classify, visualize different vocal types — song bouts begging calls — within continuous recording. tutorial walks complete LYS workflow using zebra finch dataset spanning posthatch days 661–667. Along way see : Explore single WAV file design vocalization templates interactively. Pool recordings across sessions create LYS object batch processing. Detect general audio activity run template-based vocalization detection. Label detected clips using rule-based logic. Visualize labeled vocalizations session ethogram sliding-window animation. Prerequisites: LYS requires ASAP package spectrogram visualization audio clipping.
code: library(LYS) #> Loaded LYS version 0.1.0

title: Animate Vocalization Sessions with Sliding Window — animate_vocalization_sessions
text: Creates dynamic animation displays sliding time window recording session, revealing temporal structure labeled vocalizations. Sessions scroll independently — runs end. Sequence rules allow following events reclassified visually. example, SongBout immediately follows BeggingCall displayed "FD" (Feeding-Directed) bar distinct color, optional arrow marking gap two events.

title: Animate Vocalization Sessions with Sliding Window — animate_vocalization_sessions
text: lys LYS object processed map_vocalization_sessions(). labels Character vector vocalization labels display. NULL (default), labels session map used. label_col Column name session map holding vocalization label.  Default "vocalization_label". drop_labels Character vector labels exclude display. Default "TBD". sequence_rules data frame defining sequence-based reclassification rules.  row describes one rule: preceding_label — label first event (e.g. "BeggingCall") following_label — label second event (e.g. "SongBout") max_gap_sec     — maximum gap seconds end preceding event start following event annotation      — display label reclassified following event (e.g. "FD"). label also appears legend. color           — (optional) color reclassified bar arrow. Default "#D32F2F". show_arrow      — (optional) logical, whether draw arrow gap two events. Default TRUE. NULL (default), reclassification performed. window_duration_min Numeric. Width sliding window minutes. Default 10. step_seconds Numeric. far window advances per animation frame (seconds).  Default 30. max_session_sec Numeric NULL. Maximum total duration (seconds) shown every session.  sessions clipped value end point animation. NULL (default) — use duration shortest session, every session reaches natural end frame. positive number — clip every session many seconds (e.g. 3600 1 hour). Events start cap excluded; events overlap cap boundary shown truncated. colors Named character vector mapping display labels colors. Include base labels (e.g. "SongBout") annotation labels (e.g. "FD") want override auto-assigned colors. NULL (default), colors generated automatically. fps Integer. Frames per second output animation. Default 10. output_dir Character. Directory animation file saved. NULL, uses default LYS output directory. output_file Character. File name saved animation. Default "vocalization_session_animation.gif". width Integer. Width animation frame pixels. Default 1800. height Integer. Height animation frame pixels. Default NULL (auto-calculated number sessions). res Integer. Resolution (PPI) frame.  Default 200. show_progress Logical. Show gray session progress label ("session [elapsed / total]")?  Default FALSE. verbose Logical. Print progress messages?  Default TRUE.

title: Animate Vocalization Sessions with Sliding Window — animate_vocalization_sessions

title: Apply Sequence Rules to Annotate Vocalizations — annotate_vocalizations
text: lys LYS object processed map_vocalization_sessions(). sequence_rules data frame defining sequence-based reclassification rules. Rules evaluated order appear vocalization. Required columns: preceding_label — label first event (e.g., "BeggingCall"). Use NA match unconditionally without preceding event requirement. following_label — label event reclassified (e.g., "SongBout"). max_gap_sec     — maximum gap seconds end preceding event start following event. Use NA Inf upper limit. annotation      — new label assign following event (e.g., "PD SongBout"). Optional column: min_gap_sec     — minimum gap seconds. Default 0. label_col Column name session map holding original vocalization label. Default "vocalization_label".

title: Apply Sequence Rules to Annotate Vocalizations — annotate_vocalizations
text: LYS object new data frame lys$vocalization_annotations containing annotated vocalization events. new labels stored annotated_label column, alongside original labels.

title: Apply Sequence Rules to Annotate Vocalizations — annotate_vocalizations
text: function iterates events session chronologically. event matching following_label rules, looks back recent event matching preceding_label. gap preceding event's offset current event's onset falls within [min_gap_sec, max_gap_sec], event reclassified annotation. evaluation chronological, newly reclassified events can immediately serve preceding events subsequent rules.

title: Compute Onset Latency Distribution Between Vocalization Pairs — compute_onset_latency
text: every occurrence preceding_label, finds nearest subsequent following_label event whose onset falls within window_sec preceding event's offset.  Returns tidy data frame latencies can used directly plotting statistical analysis.

title: Compute Onset Latency Distribution Between Vocalization Pairs — compute_onset_latency
code: compute_onset_latency(   data,   preceding_label,   following_label,   label_col = "vocalization_label",   start_col = "session_relative_start",   end_col = "session_relative_end",   session_col = "session_label",   window_sec = 60,   require_adjacent = TRUE )

title: Compute Onset Latency Distribution Between Vocalization Pairs — compute_onset_latency
text: data data frame vocalization events — typically lys$vocalization_session_map map_vocalization_sessions(). preceding_label Character. Label first (trigger) event. following_label Character. Label event whose onset latency measured. label_col Character. Column data holding event label. Default "vocalization_label". start_col Character. Column holding event start time (seconds). Default "session_relative_start". end_col Character. Column holding event end time (seconds). Default "session_relative_end". session_col Character. Column used group events independent sessions — pairs formed within session. Default "session_label". window_sec Numeric. Maximum time (seconds) offset preceding event onset following event. Default 60. require_adjacent Logical. TRUE (default), intervening event type preceding_label pair invalidates match (.e. SongBout must next relevant event BeggingCall).  Set FALSE allow matching following event within window regardless intervening events.

title: Compute Onset Latency Distribution Between Vocalization Pairs — compute_onset_latency
text: data frame one row per matched pair: session Session identifier. preceding_start Start time preceding event (s). preceding_end End time (offset) preceding event (s). following_start Start time (onset) following event (s). following_end End time following event (s). latency_sec Time preceding offset following onset (s). Always \(\geq 0\) \(\leq\) window_sec. Returns empty data frame (columns) pairs found.

title: Compute Onset Latency Distribution Between Vocalization Pairs — compute_onset_latency
code: if (FALSE) { # \dontrun{ # Distribution of SongBout onset latency after BeggingCall (within 60 s) latencies <- compute_onset_latency(   data            = lys$vocalization_session_map,   preceding_label = "BeggingCall",   following_label = "SongBout",   window_sec      = 60 )  hist(latencies$latency_sec,      breaks = 30,      main   = "SongBout onset latency after BeggingCall",      xlab   = "Latency (s)")  # Across multiple sessions as a density plot if (requireNamespace("ggplot2", quietly = TRUE)) {   ggplot2::ggplot(latencies, ggplot2::aes(x = latency_sec)) +     ggplot2::geom_histogram(binwidth = 5, fill = "#1976D2", color = "white") +     ggplot2::facet_wrap(~ session) +     ggplot2::labs(       title = "BeggingCall -> SongBout onset latency",       x     = "Latency (s)", y = "Count"     ) +     ggplot2::theme_minimal() } } # }

what: Conditional Rate Ratio for Vocalization Transitions — conditional_rate_ratio
title: Conditional Rate Ratio for Vocalization Transitions — conditional_rate_ratio
text: Quantifies much (less) likely response_label events occur time window immediately following trigger_label event (foreground rate) compared background rate response_label outside windows.  ratio \(\lambda_{fg} / \lambda_{bg}\) > 1 indicates trigger elevates response rate.  95% confidence interval obtained via Poisson rate-ratio approximation.  forward (trigger -> response) reverse (response -> trigger) directions computed directional asymmetry can assessed.

title: Conditional Rate Ratio for Vocalization Transitions — conditional_rate_ratio

title: Conditional Rate Ratio for Vocalization Transitions — conditional_rate_ratio
text: data data frame vocalization events. label1 Character. First label. label2 Character. Second label. window_sec Numeric. Width foreground window (seconds) trigger event. Default 120. label_col, start_col, end_col, session_col Column name arguments defaults compute_onset_latency().

title: Conditional Rate Ratio for Vocalization Transitions — conditional_rate_ratio
text: Invisibly, list two elements (label1_to_label2 label2_to_label1), list containing: n_triggers Number trigger events. n_fg Response events observed foreground windows. t_fg_sec Total foreground exposure time (s). n_bg Response events observed outside foreground windows. t_bg_sec Total background exposure time (s). rate_fg Foreground rate (events / s). rate_bg Background rate (events / s). rate_ratio rate_fg / rate_bg. ci_low,ci_high 95% CI rate ratio. p_value Two-sided p-value (exact Poisson test).

title: Export vocalization clips to per-label subdirectories — export_vocalizations
text: rules argument data frame following columns (label required; others sensible defaults): label Character. target label string.  match_mode = "exact" must exactly match vocalization_label (including compound labels like "SongBout;BeggingCall").  match_mode = "contains" needs appear one component. match_mode Character. "exact" (default) "contains".  "contains" lets route compound-labeled clips participating label's folder simultaneously. folder Character. Subdirectory name output_dir matching clips written.  Defaults sanitised label. pad_start_sec Numeric \(\geq 0\). Seconds audio added detected onset.  Default 0. pad_end_sec Numeric \(\geq 0\). Seconds audio added detected offset.  Default 0. rules = NULL (default), one rule generated automatically every unique non-drop_labels label found lys$vocalizations, using match_mode = "exact" zero padding.

title: Export vocalization clips to per-label subdirectories — export_vocalizations
code: if (FALSE) { # \dontrun{ # 1. Default: one folder per unique label, no padding lys <- export_vocalizations(lys, output_dir = "/path/to/clips")  # 2. Export only SongBout and BeggingCall, with 0.1 s padding rules <- data.frame(   label         = c("SongBout", "BeggingCall"),   pad_start_sec = 0.1,   pad_end_sec   = 0.1 ) lys <- export_vocalizations(lys, rules = rules)  # 3. Multi-label: route compound clips to each constituent label's folder rules <- data.frame(   label      = c("SongBout", "BeggingCall"),   match_mode = "contains",     # match inside compound labels   folder     = c("songs", "calls"),   pad_start_sec = c(0.05, 0.1),   pad_end_sec   = c(0.05, 0.1) ) lys <- export_vocalizations(lys, rules = rules)  # 4. Export an exact compound label to its own folder rules <- data.frame(   label      = "SongBout;BeggingCall",   match_mode = "exact",   folder     = "co-occurring" ) lys <- export_vocalizations(lys, rules = rules) } # }
